overview: The Medford Historical Commission held public hearings on demolition delay applications, determining preferably preserved status for properties on Otis Street and Sharon Street while releasing several others for demolition. The commission also voted to lift a demolition delay on Jerome Street following design revisions and reviewed updates on Community Preservation Act projects.

items.title: 20 Otis Street Carriage House Preferably Preserved Hearing
items.summary: Voted to find the carriage house at 20 Otis Street preferably preserved, imposing a demolition delay.

items.title: 76 Sharon Street Preferably Preserved Hearing
items.summary: Found the property at 76 Sharon Street preferably preserved in a 3-2 vote, placing the partial demolition project under a demolition delay.

items.title: 80 Canal Street Application Acceptance
items.summary: Accepted the demolition application for 80 Canal Street, automatically scheduling it for a preferably preserved hearing because it sits within a National Register historic district.

items.title: 10 Newcomb Street Historical Significance Hearing
items.summary: Determined that 10 Newcomb Street is not historically significant, releasing the property for total demolition.

items.title: 85 Fern Road Historical Significance Hearing
items.summary: Found 85 Fern Road not historically significant, releasing the building for proposed redevelopment.

items.title: 2-4 Capen Street Historical Significance Hearing
items.summary: Determined 2-4 Capen Street is not historically significant, allowing a proposed Tufts University student housing project to proceed.

items.title: 50 Winthrop Street Historical Significance Hearing
items.summary: Found 50 Winthrop Street not historically significant, permitting Tufts University to replace the structure with student housing.

items.title: 69 Jerome Street Demolition Delay Lift
items.summary: Voted to lift the demolition delay for 69 Jerome Street after approving revised architectural plans.

items.title: Commission Business, CPA Updates, and Minutes
items.summary: Reviewed progress on the Thomas Brooks Park archaeological dig, discussed neighborhood survey work and defense of the demolition delay ordinance, and approved the June 2022 meeting minutes.
